design_rationale:
WORKLOG — checking_fees_overdraft_and_disputes, task 0 (Marisol Etheridge, Premier Checking closure)

STEP 0. DIFFICULTY PRE-CHECK, ASSET LEDGER AND SCOPE CLAIM
Read first: references/product_extended.yaml, references/task_tools.py, references/task.json; then blueprint.yaml,
products/checking.yaml, db_schema.json and share_tools.py. Base closes: the Personal Checking charter carries six
tiers with complete parameter sets, nineteen base policies and the eleven write event types this difficulty claims.
Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0 is the first). Claimed by this task: the three extended policies
checking_ext_fee_schedule_correction, checking_ext_dispute_credit_reversal and checking_ext_closure_payout, and the
three task tools post_fee_schedule_correction_961f83a2, post_dispute_credit_reversal_956f6db8 and
confirm_closure_payout_0546356c. Left for task 1 (four problems by its own draw): the courtesy-waiver ground of
checking_evt_fee_refund, the temporary-credit posting side of checking_evt_electronic_dispute, the overdraft
protection link of checking_evt_overdraft_protection_transfer and the tier conversion of checking_product_change,
with four further task tools — an independent, load-bearing space that this task does not touch. Nothing is
reserved beyond that: after task 1 every extended policy of the charter is claimed exactly once.

Draw, taken by code before any of the tree or the computations was designed:
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py \
      env/regional_retail_bank/tasks/checking_fees_overdraft_and_disputes --tasks 2
  {"task": 0, "key": "regional_retail_bank/checking_fees_overdraft_and_disputes/0", "prerequisite_problems": 2,
   "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 4]}
  {"task": 1, "key": "regional_retail_bank/checking_fees_overdraft_and_disputes/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3,
   "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4, 4]}
Task 0 therefore has exactly two prerequisite problems and each of its three computations carries exactly four
declared factors: checking_ext_fee_schedule_correction 4, checking_ext_dispute_credit_reversal 4,
checking_ext_closure_payout 4. The design was fitted to the draw, never the other way round.

DESIGN THESIS. Surface goal: "close the checking account and move what is left into my money market." Scored core
parameter: payout_amount on the owner's own closing step. Between the two lies a chain of two policy prerequisites
that the customer never mentions. The closing payout is reconciled out of the account's own entries, and the rule
of checking_ext_closure_payout says outright that it "is worked out only once every temporary credit standing on
the account for a claim decided in the bank's own favour has been taken back on the ledger" — a state the records
show false, because the claim of 2025-06-06 reads resolved_bank_favor while its 2145.00 temporary credit still
stands unreversed. Working out that take-back leads to checking_ext_dispute_credit_reversal, whose own rule says
the amount "is settled only after the ledger carries a corrective entry against every overdraft charge standing
above the published fee schedule" — again false, because three of the five June overdraft charges were taken at
42.00, 38.50 and 24.50 where Premier Checking's schedule produces 35.00 for each chargeable item, and no entry
stands against any of them. That is the whole chain: correction, take-back, payout. Depth: three problems, one
order. Breadth: each of the three computations reads this account's ledger history, the owner's money market
balance, her certificate principal and twelve months of her card payment history, and each of the three is decided
by four ladders over those records. The customer names none of it.

STEP 0 CARD 1 — BASE-INVARIANT CARD (per exact write subject)
checking_fee_refund (the corrective entry, step 10). Governing base policies: checking_evt_fee_refund and
checking_evt_electronic_dispute.
  eligible_fee_code (authorization, system_record, pre_action, correlated on checking_transactions.checking_txn_id
    bound to the call's source_item_id): the corrected charge carries fee_code overdraft_item, which is the third
    entry of courtesy_eligible_fee_codes. Satisfied.
  courtesy_window (time). Starting business event: "The fee must have posted". Authoritative anchor:
    checking_transactions.posted_date. Clock: frozen_time. Duration source: variants.courtesy_refund_window_days,
    90 for Premier Checking. Counting rule, verbatim: "Count calendar days with the day after the fee's posted_date
    as day 1; the refund is allowed while the frozen date is on or before the fee's posted_date plus
    courtesy_refund_window_days." Direction: not_after. Boundary: inclusive. Positive case: the charge posted
    2025-06-27, and 2025-06-27 plus 90 days is 2025-09-25, well after the frozen date of 2025-07-18. Negative case:
    a charge posted 2025-04-18 gives 2025-07-17, one day short, and the courtesy ground would be closed. Boundary
    case: a charge posted 2025-04-19 gives exactly 2025-07-18, still open because the boundary is inclusive.
  courtesy_limit (authorization, correlated on checking_transactions.customer_id bound to the call's customer_id):
    Premier Checking allows three courtesy refunds in a rolling 365 days; the owner's seeded activity carries no
    entry with adjustment_reason courtesy_waiver at all, so the count is zero. Satisfied.
  account_active (state, correlated on checking_accounts.checking_account_id): status is active at the frozen date
    and the account is not closed until step 14. Satisfied.
  refund_once (dedup, object_bindings {source_item_id: source_item_id}, duplicate_filters event_type
    checking_fee_refund): no refund-kind entry of any ground stands against the 42.00 charge. Satisfied.
  checking_evt_electronic_dispute has no eligibility whose applies_to reaches checking_fee_refund, so it is carried
    as policy_scope: it governs the dispute_final ground, which this bank-error entry is not.
checking_provisional_reversal (the take-back, step 12). Governing base policy: checking_evt_electronic_dispute, whose
  single gate on this subject, reversal_needs_bank_favor, is superseded clause by clause by this task's
  checking_ext_dispute_credit_reversal (see the overwrite below); the extended rule carries the bank-favour
  requirement itself in its own words, so nothing is lost. Carried as policy_scope.
checking_close (the closing payout, step 14). Governing base policy: checking_evt_closure.
  balance_not_negative (authorization, correlated on checking_accounts.checking_account_id): at the handling time of
    step 14 the posted ledger balance is 4666.97 — the seeded 6416.22 plus the 144.25 correction less the 1893.50
    take-back — so it is above zero. Note that the order matters here in one direction only: the take-back never
    drives the balance below zero because the take-back itself is bounded by what stands as a temporary credit.
  no_open_dispute (authorization, correlated on checking_disputes.checking_account_id): the two claims on the
    account read resolved_customer_favor and resolved_bank_favor; neither is submitted and neither is
    provisional_credited, so the closure is not blocked. Satisfied.
  early_window (time) has applies_to [checking_fee] only and is therefore not a precondition of a checking_close
    write; the closing charge it governs is folded into the payout by the declared overwrite below, so no separate
    charge entry is owed and no obligation is left hanging.
Automatic clauses of base checked against this seed: the monthly maintenance fee is assessed at cycle close and is
waived for Premier Checking by a minimum daily balance at or above 10000.00 or a relationship balance at or above
25000.00 — the owner's money market alone carries 54200.00, so no maintenance fee is owed and none is seeded; the
paper statement fee is 0.00 for the tier and delivery is electronic; the account has never closed a day below zero,
so negative_since_date is empty and neither the extended overdraft fee nor the restriction clock is running;
last_customer_activity_date is 2025-07-16, so dormancy is nowhere near; the tier pays interest, which is why the
closing payout carries a closing-interest term rather than ignoring it.

STEP 0 CARD 2 — BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
Target object of the corrective entry: the single overdraft charge of 42.00 posted 2025-06-27 on this checking
account. Correlation key: checking_transactions.checking_txn_id, written into the new entry's source_item_id. Rows
that enter the aggregate: the five overdraft charges posted 2025-06-27 (42.00, 38.50, 35.00, 35.00, 24.50), which
are the charges inside the one-month review window. Rows excluded: the two overdraft charges of 35.00 posted
2025-05-14, whose posted date puts them a whole month or more before the frozen date; they are visible in the same
lookup and are exactly the near-miss a careless reader sums in. Nothing has been settled against any of the seven.
Target object of the take-back: the temporary credit of 2145.00 posted 2025-06-11, correlated by its own
checking_txn_id into source_item_id and by checking_dispute_id to the claim of 2025-06-06. Rows that enter: that
credit alone, because only it lies inside the two-month claim window. Row excluded: the temporary credit of 310.00
posted 2025-05-09, which belongs to the other claim — the one decided in the owner's favour, where the rule says
expressly the credit "becomes final where it stands". Target object of the closing payout: the checking account
itself; the aggregate is every entry booked to it, and the destination is correlated by
checking_closure_requests.destination_account_id and the paying-out entry's counterparty_account_id to the money
market holding.

STEP 0 CARD 3 — PROBLEM-TREE CARD
  root: checking_ext_closure_payout (target_tool confirm_closure_payout_0546356c, owner=user)
     <- checking_ext_dispute_credit_reversal (post_dispute_credit_reversal_956f6db8, owner=agent)
        <- checking_ext_fee_schedule_correction (post_fee_schedule_correction_961f83a2, owner=agent)
Edge 1 (closure payout waits on the take-back). kind value_input; gate takebacks_out, a real compute binding of
checking_ext_closure_payout; form state. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the blocked policy's own rule: "The
closing payout is worked out only once every temporary credit standing on the account for a claim decided in the
bank's own favour has been taken back on the ledger." Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only once",
joining this policy's own result, the closing payout, to what it waits on; (2) the side it waits on is a
record-visible state — a take-back entry standing on the ledger against a temporary credit — and names no action,
no performer and no tool; (3) it carries no tool name, no policy id and no snake_case or hexadecimal token; (4) its
strength is exactly the edge's: "only once ... has been taken back" is a hard requirement, and its scope, temporary
credits on claims decided the bank's way, is precisely the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings
that state about: post_dispute_credit_reversal_956f6db8 is the only tool in task_tools.py that creates an entry of
the take-back kind, and checking_ext_dispute_credit_reversal is the only policy whose result is such an entry.
Derivation the reader performs: the sentence says the payout waits on take-back entries standing for claims decided
the bank's way; the dispute lookup shows the 2025-06-06 claim reading resolved_bank_favor; the activity lookup
shows a 2145.00 temporary credit for it and no entry of the take-back kind anywhere on the account; the rule of
checking_ext_dispute_credit_reversal says a temporary credit "is taken back once that claim stands decided in the
bank's own favour or has been withdrawn by the owner" — so the one action that brings the waited-on state about is
that policy's take-back, and there is no second reading. Seed evidence that it is false at the opening:
initial_state.checking_disputes.<claim 2>.dispute_status = resolved_bank_favor;
initial_state.checking_transactions.<credit 2>.adjustment_reason = dispute_provisional and .amount = 2145.00; no
row of the account carries event_type checking_provisional_reversal, so the takebacks_out binding evaluates to 0.00.
Edge 2 (take-back waits on the corrective entry). kind value_input; gate corrections_standing, a real compute
binding of checking_ext_dispute_credit_reversal; form state. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from that policy's own
rule: "The amount taken back is settled only after the ledger carries a corrective entry against every overdraft
charge standing above the published fee schedule." Four-point test: (1) "only after" is the ordering connective and
the result it governs is this policy's own, the amount taken back; (2) the side it waits on is the record-visible
state of a corrective entry standing on the ledger, with no action, performer or tool named; (3) no tool name, no
policy id, no code token; (4) "only after ... every" is a hard requirement over exactly the charges the edge's
condition names. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about:
post_fee_schedule_correction_961f83a2 is the only tool that creates a refund-kind entry on the bank-error ground,
and checking_ext_fee_schedule_correction is the only policy whose result is such an entry. Derivation: the sentence
says the take-back waits on corrective entries standing against overdraft charges above the schedule; the activity
lookup shows five June charges of 42.00, 38.50, 35.00, 35.00 and 24.50 while the account lookup shows Premier
Checking, whose overdraft fee for each item is 35.00, so three of them stand above the schedule; no refund-kind
entry stands against any of them; the rule of checking_ext_fee_schedule_correction says the bank "puts the
difference back as one corrective entry on the bank-error ground" — one action, one reading. Seed evidence that it
is false at the opening: initial_state.checking_transactions.<charge 42.00>.amount = 42.00 and .adjustment_reason =
none, .<charge 38.50>.amount = 38.50, .<charge 24.50>.amount = 24.50, and the account carries no row with
event_type checking_fee_refund, so the corrections_standing binding evaluates to 0.00.
Topological order: fee schedule correction, then credit reversal, then closure payout — the only order the chain
admits. There are no parallel edges, so nothing can be reordered and order_uniqueness is settled by the shape of
the tree rather than by a commuting argument. Per-edge deletion sensitivity, from the Step 5 run: skipping the
corrective entry moves the scored reversal_amount from 1893.50 to 2040.00; skipping the take-back moves the scored
payout_amount from 4658.30 to 6552.03. Neither edge is decorative. user_scenario mentions no prerequisite problem
and no part of either (see no_user_hint). The tool layer validates nothing (see tools_do_not_block).
Customer's own write: the root problem. confirm_closure_payout_0546356c is declared @tool(owner="user"), the agent
unlocks it with unlock_user_discoverable_tool at action 13 and the simulator runs it at action 14. The in-person
semantics are the blueprint's own: "confirming an account closure" is listed there among the owner's own consent,
and the persona gives the reason in character. It completes on the spot — the closing instruction, the paying-out
entry and the closure of the account are all written by that one call under the same frozen clock.

STEP 1 — POLICIES WRITTEN, AND THE OVERRIDES DECLARED
checking_ext_fee_schedule_correction. base_policy_refs: checking_evt_fee_refund and checking_evt_electronic_dispute
(the two base policies governing checking_fee_refund) plus checking_evt_overdraft_and_returned_item_fees as genuine
input lineage, because the schedule the correction is measured against is that policy's. overwrite: one entry,
naming checking_evt_fee_refund and superseding the clause "whose amount equals that fee's amount" with this
policy's own sentence "The corrective entry is the charges under review less the charge the schedule produces,
never below zero." Evaluating the same quantity twice in the same world shows why the declaration is needed: base
would put back 42.00, the full charge; this policy puts back 144.25 across the run of charges. The clause is a
substring of the base rule and is contained in no eligibility condition, so no gate is retired by it. trigger
state_due: at a month-end reconciliation, with no customer calling, the bank already owes this money back, because
the charges standing above the schedule are a bank error the charter itself calls out.
checking_ext_dispute_credit_reversal. base_policy_refs: checking_evt_electronic_dispute. overwrite: one entry
superseding "for the full provisional credit amount" with "The amount taken back is the temporary credit standing
on the account, netted against the corrective entries the bank has already made, less the part left with the
owner, and never below zero." Base would take back 2145.00; this policy takes back 1893.50 — different, so the
declaration is required. That clause is part of the sentence carrying the reversal_needs_bank_favor gate, so the
gate is retired by the declaration; the extended rule restates the substance in its own first sentence ("is taken
back once that claim stands decided in the bank's own favour or has been withdrawn by the owner") and closes the
domain with "A claim that stands decided in the owner's favour is outside this rule and its temporary credit
becomes final where it stands." trigger state_due: the bank is owed this back whether or not the owner calls.
checking_ext_closure_payout. base_policy_refs: checking_evt_closure and checking_evt_interest, both of which this
policy supersedes clause by clause. overwrite: seven entries. Four against checking_evt_closure, each naming the base
sentence it retires and the sentence of this rule that takes its place — the two-step register-then-confirm procedure becomes
the owner's single confirmation; the separately booked early closure fee becomes a charge taken out of the money
paid out; the separately credited closing interest becomes a term added to the money paid out; and the bare "the
remaining ledger balance is disbursed in full" becomes the reconciled figure less the charge and with the interest.
None of the four contains or is contained in balance_not_negative, no_open_dispute or early_window, so all three
gates stay in force and the first two are carried item by item in the contract. Three further entries against
checking_evt_interest declare what the closing interest replaces of that policy's own method, because naming
checking_evt_interest in base_policy_refs while changing how much the interest is — and not only where it lands —
is a conflict that has to be declared sentence by sentence or the base method stays in force alongside it. The
daily accrual sentence is retired by this policy's single-figure method sentence; the band-selection sentence,
which picks the APY of the highest band floor the balance reaches, is retired by this policy's closing-rate
ladder, which selects on the owner's card payments and premier money market balance instead; and the sentence that sums
the daily amounts over the cycle and credits them as their own entry is retired by the sentence that adds the
closing interest to the money paid out. Evaluating the same quantity twice in the same world is what shows the
declarations are needed: base's own method takes the balance band of 4666.97, which is the 0.00 floor at 0.02 per
cent, and yields 0.08, where this policy yields 0.58. checking_evt_interest carries no eligibility, so no gate is
retired by any of the three, and the policy's governing lineage for a checking_close write is unchanged. trigger on_request: with no
customer calling, no closing payout falls due; it arises only because she asks for the account closed.
Two-way sweep, rule -> compute_basis -> compute, done binding by binding: every binding that reads the world,
aggregates, chooses a tier, crosses a category, caps or rounds carries a verbatim quotation of the rule sentence
that legislates it, recorded in compute_basis; the reverse sweep read each rule through and found a binding for
every promise it makes about a quantity, a window, a filter, a branch, an acting base, an ordering, a cap or a
rounding. Two examples of the pinning the sweep forced: in checking_ext_dispute_credit_reversal the rule states
that the netting "is worked out on the corrective entries standing and rounded half-up to the cent before it is
taken off" and that the part left with the owner "is worked out on the temporary credit standing and rounded
half-up to the cent, and it is taken off after the netting" — so the two subtractions act on different bases and
each names its own, the order of the two is fixed, and the rounding moment is named for each; in checking_ext_closure_payout
the rule states that the closing interest is "the money reconciled from the account's own entries multiplied by the
closing rate as an annual percentage, multiplied by the closing days and divided by three hundred and sixty-five,
rounded half-up to the cent; the closing days are the days the account has been open, capped at one full statement
cycle", which pins the base, the day-count convention, the cap and the rounding moment without any summary word.

STEP 1 — FACTOR CARD (four declared factors per computation; the drawn count)
checking_ext_fee_schedule_correction
  chargeable_item_allowance, parameter, cross-difficulty savings, multi-source. Ladder: premier money market balance at or
    above the tier's relationship maintenance threshold AND at least four overdraft charges standing -> the deep
    relationship allowance of one item; premier money market balance at or above the protection source minimum OR at least
    eight card payments in twelve months -> the relationship allowance of two items; otherwise the tier's
    chargeable-item limit. Tier taken here: the first, on the money market row carrying 54200.00 against Premier
    Checking's 25000.00 threshold, and five charges standing. Baseline reading: the tier's limit of three, giving
    82.75 instead of 144.25.
  per_item_charge_level, parameter, cross-difficulty card, multi-source. Ladder: at least ten card payments in
    twelve months AND at least four charges standing -> the tier's overdraft fee for each item less the deep
    relationship reduction; at least four card payments OR premier money market balance at or above the protection source
    minimum -> that fee less the relationship reduction; otherwise the fee itself. Tier taken: the first, on the
    twelve card payments seeded between 2024-08-05 and 2025-07-05. Baseline reading: 35.00, giving 140.00.
  charges_under_review_basis, method. Ladder: premier money market balance at or above the relationship maintenance
    threshold AND at least four charges standing -> only the charges inside the review window are summed; at least
    two charges standing OR at least twenty card payments -> only the largest single charge is taken; otherwise
    every overdraft charge whenever posted is summed. Tier taken: the first, giving 175.00. Baseline reading:
    245.00, giving 214.25. The near-miss lives here: the two 35.00 charges of 2025-05-14 are visible in the same
    lookup and are excluded by the window alone.
  corrective_entry_rounding, method, cross-difficulty cd. Ladder: certificate principal at or above the certificate
    relationship minimum AND at least four charges standing -> to the cent; any certificate principal OR at least
    fifteen card payments -> whole dollars; otherwise whole five-dollar steps. Tier taken: the first, on the
    60000.00 certificate. Baseline reading: five-dollar steps, giving 145.00.
  Whole-baseline fall-back: 140.00, against a gold of 144.25.
checking_ext_dispute_credit_reversal
  temporary_credit_measure, method, cross-difficulty card. Tier taken: only the credits inside the two-month claim
    window, 2145.00. Baseline: every credit less every take-back, 2455.00, giving 2188.00. Near-miss: the 310.00
    credit of 2025-05-09, which sits one day outside the window and belongs to the claim decided the owner's way.
  corrective_entry_netting, parameter, cross-difficulty savings, multi-source. Tier taken: the whole share, on the
    premier money market balance and the corrective entry now standing. Baseline: no netting, giving 2037.75.
  owner_retained_share, parameter, cross-difficulty cd, multi-source. Tier taken: the deep relationship share of
    five per cent, on the 60000.00 certificate and twelve card payments. Baseline: nothing retained, giving 2000.75.
  take_back_rounding, method. Tier taken: to the cent, on the corrective entry granted in the last twelve months
    together with the certificate principal. Baseline: five-dollar steps, giving 1895.00.
  Whole-baseline fall-back: 2455.00, against a gold of 1893.50.
checking_ext_closure_payout
  closing_charge_level_band, parameter, cross-difficulty savings, multi-source. Tier taken: the tier's early
    closure charge less the relationship charge relief, 18.50. Baseline: 25.00, giving 4655.05.
  closing_charge_basis, method, cross-difficulty cd. Tier taken: spread evenly over the two whole months the account
    has been open — 28 April to 28 May and 28 May to 28 June, the third not yet having come round on 18 July — 9.25. Baseline: taken in full at the level set, giving 4649.05.
  closing_rate_band, parameter, cross-difficulty card, multi-source. Tier taken: the premier relationship rate of
    0.15 per cent. Baseline: the base account rate of 0.02 per cent, giving 4657.80.
  closing_payout_rounding, method. Tier taken: to the cent. Baseline: five-dollar steps, giving 4660.00.
  Whole-baseline fall-back: 4640.00, against a gold of 4658.30.
No base boundary was weakened to make room for any of these: every tier value is the tier's own parameter, this
policy's declared params, or an arithmetic on them, and no second product law was created.

STEP 3 — WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS
The customer profile and the checking account carry the identity the desk verifies and the tier every ladder reads.
The eight credit entries (the 900.00 opening deposit, the 900.00 rebate check and six payroll credits of 2482.60)
and the thirteen paid items give the account a real two-and-a-half-month shape and make the reconciliation of the
closing payout genuine: delete any one of them and payout_amount moves. The two overdraft charges of 2025-05-14
exist to be excluded by the review window; delete them and charges_under_review_basis stops biting, since its
baseline reading would then equal its gold reading. The five charges of 2025-06-27 at 42.00, 38.50, 35.00, 35.00
and 24.50 are the schedule error the correction turns on; delete the three off-schedule ones and the corrective
entry has nothing to put back. The temporary credit of 310.00 from 2025-05-09 exists to be excluded by the claim
window and by the owner-favour clause; delete it and temporary_credit_measure becomes decoration. The temporary
credit of 2145.00 and its claim reading resolved_bank_favor are the take-back's object. The money market
(54200.00), the certificate (60000.00) and the twelve card payments are the cross-product evidence three ladders
each rest on: drop the money market and the chargeable-item allowance, the netting share and the closing charge
level all fall to their fall-through tiers; drop the certificate and the rounding of the corrective entry, the part
left with the owner and the way the closing charge is taken all fall; drop the card payments and the per-item
charge, the temporary credit measure and the closing rate all fall. Cache design check: no event-statistic cache
field is used as a trap in this task — checking_accounts.ledger_balance is kept exactly equal to the reconciled sum
of the seeded entries (6416.22) so that the account row and the ledger agree, and the difficulty comes from
reconciling the entries at handling time rather than from a stale figure. Automatic-clause check: see the
base-invariant card — no maintenance fee, no paper statement fee, no extended overdraft fee, no dormancy and no
restriction is owed on this world, so the task set carries no obligation it does not discharge.

STEP 4 — THE PERSONA
Voice: brisk, warm, slightly impatient; she is calling on a break and says so, and the tone is that of someone
tidying up rather than complaining. Volunteered at the opening: her name, the mobile number, the rehearsed request
to close the checking account and move what is left into the money market, the fact that she opened the account at
the end of April, and the fact that she does not know the closing figure. Every one of those points at a seeded
row: the opening date 2025-04-28 on the account, the mobile number on the profile, the money market holding.
Given only when asked: date of birth, Social Security last four, ZIP, email, the date she first banked with
Piedmont Crescent, and her preference between a transfer and a mailed check. Explicit cannot-answer branch: she
does not know any internal reference number and says so, which is why every reference number in gold comes from a
lookup return. Passive reactions, each tied to an utterance event the agent produces rather than to a database
state: when the agent explains that something has to go onto the account before the closing figure can be settled,
she says go ahead and does not ask what it is; when the agent hands her the closing step, she completes it; when
she hears the account is closed and the money has gone across, she thanks the agent and rings off. The natural trap
is the re-check line — if a figure strikes her as thin she asks for it to be checked against the account and offers
no figure of her own. Nothing in the text names either prerequisite problem, the claims, the overdraft charges or
any computed value, and the arc closes exactly where evaluation_criteria closes: her last reaction answers the last
gold action and asks for nothing beyond it.

STEP 5 — VERIFICATION CODE, COMMANDS AND OUTPUT
The verification harness topologically sorts the tree, replays the gold writes with the real share and task tools
onto the seeded database, and evaluates each policy's ordered bindings on the world standing just before its own
write; it then runs the per-factor baseline substitution, the whole-baseline substitution and the per-edge skip.
Commands actually run from the repository root:
  .venv/bin/python <scratch>/cprobe0.py
Output:
  == corr 144.25 rev 1893.5 pay 4658.3
  checking_ext_fee_schedule_correction gold 144.25 baseline_all 140.0
       chargeable_item_allowance 82.75
       per_item_charge_level 140.0
       charges_under_review_basis 214.25
       corrective_entry_rounding 145.0
  checking_ext_dispute_credit_reversal gold 1893.5 baseline_all 2455.0
       temporary_credit_measure 2188.0
       corrective_entry_netting 2037.75
       owner_retained_share 2000.75
       take_back_rounding 1895.0

Marisol Etheridge is thirty-nine and runs the scheduling desk at a physical-therapy group off Battleground Avenue in Greensboro. She is friendly but in a hurry, calling on her break and saying so, and she has decided she is carrying one account too many. She opened this checking account at the end of April when her old bank shut the branch she used, never really settled into it, and keeps everything in her money market anyway. So she opens with the whole of it: her name, the mobile number 3365550118 the bank has for her, and the sentence she has clearly rehearsed on the drive in, please close the checking account and move what is left into my money market. She does not know what the closing figure is and says so cheerfully; she has not looked at the account in weeks and she is not going to guess at it.

She will answer whatever the desk needs to be sure it is her. Asked to confirm her date of birth she gives 1986-04-12. Asked for the last four of her Social Security number she gives 1147. Asked for the ZIP on file she gives 27455. She will give her email or the date she first banked with Piedmont Crescent too if either is asked for, but she volunteers none of it unprompted. She does not know any internal reference numbers and says so plainly if she is asked for one; the account she means is the checking one, and the money market is the only savings account she has ever had here.

On who does what she is clear without being asked twice. Whatever entries the desk has to make on the account itself, she is content for them to make on her behalf, and she does not want a running commentary on each one. The one thing she wants to do in person is give the final word that closes the account; she says her mother lost an account to a mix-up once and she has been careful ever since. So when the agent explains that something has to go onto the account before the closing figure can be settled, she says go ahead and does not ask what it is. When the agent tells her the desk is ready and hands the closing step over to her, she takes it and completes it herself there and then.

Asked where the money should go, she says into the money market, the one she has had for years, and if the agent presses her for a number she asks them to read back which one they mean rather than reciting digits. Asked whether she would rather have a check in the post, she says no, a transfer is simpler. If the agent offers her a closing figure beforehand and it strikes her as thin, she will only say that does not sound like what I had in there, would you check it against the account, and leave it there; she has no figure of her own and will not invent one.

Once she hears that the account is closed and the money has gone across to the money market, she is done. She thanks the agent, says that is one less thing to think about, and rings off. She asks for nothing after that.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.correction_amount: 144.25. The overdraft charges standing on the account are seven: two of 35.00 posted 2025-05-14 and five posted 2025-06-27 of 42.00, 38.50, 35.00, 35.00 and 24.50. The premier money market balance of 54200.00 reaches Premier Checking's relationship maintenance threshold of 25000.00 and seven overdraft charges stand on the account, so only the five posted inside the one-month review window count toward the charges under review and they come to 175.00; the May pair falls outside the window. The same pair of conditions puts the chargeable-item allowance on its deep relationship tier of one item rather than Premier Checking's limit of three. Twelve card payments stand in the last twelve months and at least four overdraft charges stand, so each chargeable item is charged at Premier Checking's overdraft fee for each item, 35.00, less the deep relationship reduction of 4.25, that is 30.75. The charge the schedule produces is 30.75 multiplied by the smaller of five and one, so 30.75, and the corrective entry is 175.00 less 30.75, that is 144.25. The certificate principal of 60000.00 reaches the certificate relationship minimum of 25000.00 and at least four charges stand, so the entry is taken to the cent rather than in whole dollars or whole five-dollar steps.

Uniqueness: the charges under review are 42.00, 38.50, 35.00, 35.00 and 24.50, so the largest is unique, and the two May charges are outside the review window and cannot be it.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.payout_amount: 4658.30. The money reconciled from the account's own entries at this step is 4666.97: credits of 14213.00 in deposits, 144.25 in the corrective entry and 2455.00 in temporary credits, less debits of 10006.78 in paid items, 245.00 in charges and 1893.50 in the take-back. The premier money market balance reaches Premier Checking's relationship maintenance threshold and the account has been open 81 days, past the settled account period of 60, so the closing charge is set at the tier's early closure charge of 25.00 less the relationship charge relief of 6.50, that is 18.50. The certificate principal reaches the certificate relationship minimum and the account is past the settled account period, so that 18.50 is spread evenly over the whole months the account has been open: from the opening date of 2025-04-28 the day of the month has come round on 2025-05-28 and 2025-06-28 but not again before the frozen date of 2025-07-18, so the count is two and 18.50 divided by two is 9.25. Twelve card payments stand in the last twelve months and the premier money market balance reaches the relationship maintenance threshold, so the closing rate is the premier relationship rate of 0.15 per cent; the closing days are 81 capped at one full statement cycle of 30, so the closing interest is 4666.97 times 0.0015 times 30 divided by 365, that is 0.58. A corrective entry has been granted in the last twelve months and the account is past the settled account period, so the payout is taken to the cent: 4666.97 less 9.25 plus 0.58.

edges.condition: The account's posted activity carries a take-back entry against every temporary credit that stands on it for a claim whose decision went the bank's way.
edges.policy_source: The closing payout is worked out only once every temporary credit standing on the account for a claim decided in the bank's own favour has been taken back on the ledger.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain, not a fan-out: the closing payout waits on the take-back and the take-back waits on the corrective entry, so there is exactly one topological order and nothing can be reordered. The run recorded under edge_load_bearing confirms the chain is real in both directions: with the corrective entry skipped the take-back recomputes to 2040.00 instead of 1893.50, and with the take-back skipped the closing payout recomputes to 6552.03 instead of 4658.30.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the take-back and replaying everything else leaves the money reconciled from the account's own entries at 6560.47 rather than 4666.97, and the scored payout_amount recomputes to 6552.03 instead of 4658.30; the terminal state also loses the 1893.50 debit entry entirely.

Skipping the corrective entry and replaying everything else drops the corrections standing binding to 0.00, moves the netting tier from the whole to the half share, drops the twelve-month refund count to zero so the take-back is taken in whole five-dollar steps, and the scored reversal_amount recomputes to 2040.00 instead of 1893.50.

prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: post_dispute_credit_reversal_956f6db8 and confirm_closure_payout_0546356c both write unconditionally. Each body is a straight ctx.create plus a ctx.update on the balance (and, for the closing tool, a ctx.create of the closing instruction and a ctx.update setting status closed): neither reads the corrections standing, neither counts take-back entries, neither inspects a claim state, and neither can return an error on a business ground.
